name: a_strategist_views
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Strategists & positioning.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Named strategist and investor commentary with numbers (index targets, rate calls, sector calls), fund flows, positioning/short-interest data, sentiment gauges, research notes on market-wide themes (AI capex returns, AI productivity surveys, bubble/misallocation debates by named academics or firms).

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **SPX** / US Equities `[Macro]`
- The S&P 500 was near 8,000 after gaining 13% year to date; Julien Lafargue, chief market strategist at Barclays Private Bank, said quarterly results would need to be “very, very strong” for the index to break higher. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- RBC Capital Markets reduced US technology to **market weight** and rotated toward healthcare; Citigroup removed its **overweight** recommendation on US equities after indicators reached levels historically associated with market peaks. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- S&P 500 third-quarter earnings were expected to rise **30.6% year over year**, according to Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG; excluding the Magnificent Seven, technology and energy, HSBC estimated earnings growth at **5%**, down from **14%** in the prior quarter. (Reuters, Oct 15; publish time not provided)

## **RUT** / US Small Caps `[Macro]`
- Systematic trend-followers held their **largest net short position in the Russell 2000 since 2023**, according to a Goldman Sachs flow-of-funds update. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)

## US Equity Positioning `[Macro]`
- Goldman Sachs’s US Equity Sentiment Indicator stood at **−1.3 standard deviations**; the report said this reading historically corresponded to an average **2.0% forward one-month S&P 500 return**. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- CTA positioning in the S&P 500 was at the **27th percentile** on a one-year basis and the **54th percentile** on a five-year basis. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Approximately **10% of S&P 500 constituents** were scheduled to exit corporate buyback blackout periods during the week of Oct. 15. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- S&P 500 corporate buyback execution totaled **$1.269 trillion year to date**; technology buybacks were down **40% year over year**, while financials were up **88%**, energy **480%**, and utilities **538%**. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Money-market funds recorded **$166.37 billion of net inflows** for the week ended Oct. 7, reversing **$15.9 billion** of aggregate outflows over the preceding four weeks. (Tickmill, Oct 15; publish time not provided)

## Magnificent Seven Positioning `[Internet & Platforms]`
- Hazeltree’s September data covering more than **700 hedge funds** and approximately **16,000 securities** showed increased long participation in Alphabet, with smaller increases in Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon and Meta; short participation rose notably in Meta and Tesla. (Hedgeweek, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Tesla’s long-to-short hedge-fund holder ratio fell to **0.54**, its lowest level of 2026; Apple and Tesla were the only Magnificent Seven stocks with more short than long holders. (Hedgeweek, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Broadcom’s net-long exposure rose from **34.1% to 54.1%**, shifting the stock from short-biased to long-biased positioning in Hazeltree’s data. (Hedgeweek, Oct 15; publish time not provided)

## AI Capex and Bubble Risk `[AI Infrastructure]`
- Jim, a named market commentator in the cited Bloomberg segment, said the current AI capex cycle could extend to **2031**, when he said US tax deductibility for the spending would end; he also cited TSMC and Micron bookings extending through **2028**. (BNN Bloomberg, Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Spending by Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, SpaceX, Oracle, CoreWeave and Nebius was forecast at **$971 billion in 2026**, up from **$32 billion in 2016**, with forecasts of **$1.3 trillion in 2027** and **$1.4 trillion in 2028**. The figures were cited by AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould. (Trustnet, updated Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Bank of America’s October Global Fund Manager Survey identified global semiconductors as the most crowded trade, cited by **45%** of respondents; managers were net **37% overweight technology**, the highest reading since August 2020. (Trustnet, updated Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- Fund managers were split on an AI bubble forming in 2027: **45%** expected one and **42%** did not. (Trustnet, updated Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- **39%** of survey respondents identified hyperscaler AI capex as the most likely source of a systemic credit event, ahead of government debt at **28%** and private credit at **24%**. (Trustnet, updated Oct 15; publish time not provided)
- **57%** of fund managers did not expect AI companies to reduce capex during the following six months. (Trustnet, updated Oct 15; publish time not provided)

## US Dollar and AI Repricing `[Macro / Geopolitics]`
- Spectra Markets president Brent Donnelly said a serious repricing of the AI capex boom would be “unambiguously dollar bearish,” as AI stocks fell and concerns spread to credit markets tied to data-center profitability. (Reuters, Oct 16; publish time not provided)
